name: Ependymoblastoma
aliases: Primitive Neuroectodermal Tumor of the Central Nervous System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of multilayered rosettes on histopathological examination
Positive staining for neuronal and glial markers such as synaptophysin and GFAP
Identification of C19MC amplification or other characteristic molecular alterations
MRI showing a large, heterogeneous, well-demarcated mass often in the supratentorial region

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of multilayered rosettes combined with molecular genetic evidence of characteristic alterations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular profiling is essential to distinguish ependymoblastoma from other embryonal CNS tumors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multilayered rosette formation on tumor histology
Rapidly progressive intracranial mass effect symptoms
searchTerms: rapid onset of brain pressure signs

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Vomiting associated with raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea due to raised intracranial pressure
eye symptoms from raised brain pressure
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing

laboratory: CSF cytology typically negative for malignant cells
Elevated intracranial pressure on lumbar puncture
imaging: MRI showing large, heterogeneous supratentorial mass with cystic and solid components
Mass effect with midline shift and hydrocephalus
genetic: Distinct methylation profile separating it from other embryonal tumors
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin, GFAP, and EMA

distinguishingFeatures: Different molecular profile without C19MC amplification
Typically arises in posterior fossa or spinal cord
Distinct molecular subgroups (WNT, SHH, Group 3, Group 4)

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (severe headache, vomiting, papilledema)
New onset seizures in a young child
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Pajtler KW, et al. Molecular Classification of Ependymomas across All CNS Compartments, Histopathology, 2015.
Ramaswamy V, et al. Medulloblastoma and Embryonal Tumors: Molecular Classification and Clinical Implications, Neuro Oncol, 2016.
